messages.subject: varying coefficient model via INLA
messages.subject_clean: varying coefficient model via INLA
messages.body_plain:
Hi INLA experts,

I am wondering if we can fit a varying coefficient model via INLA. For instance, I am interested in evaluating the slope of PM2.5 values which may vary through different effect modifiers.

Model:

Y= beta1*(E1)*PM2.5+beta2(E2)*PM2.5
where E1 is effect modifier 1 and E2 is effect modifier 2, and we believe these two effect modifiers affect the relationship between PM2.5 and Y.
In addition, I want to use the P-spline approach to smooth them. Does that sound doable?

I noticed that the model includes interaction terms, and I am wondering how to specify this model using INLA code.

Many thanks!
Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Issues with INLA executables in singularity box
messages.subject_clean: Issues with INLA executables in singularity box
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am fitting a series of models through INLA in R via a HPC system.

This HPC system is very limited in the number of software it supports, so my approach has been to create a Docker image in a separate Ubuntu machine which then gets converted into a singularity image on the HPC (Docker is not allowed in the HPC system I'm using). I do not have root access on the HPC, so I need INLA to be able to run for all users.

I noticed that after INLA version 21.02.23, the default permission of some executables have changed. This is an example from a singularity box created using INLA 21.02.23

```
$ ls -lG /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/
...
-rwxrwxr-x 1 root 11989728 May  1 17:52 fmesher
-rwxrwxr-x 1 root      482 May  1 17:52 fmesher.run
-rwxrwxr-x 1 root 17712640 May  1 17:52 inla
-rwxrwxr-x 1 root 84591696 May  1 17:52 inla.mkl
-rwxrwxr-x 1 root     1384 May  1 17:52 inla.mkl.run
-rwxrwxr-x 1 root     1384 May  1 17:52 inla.run
...
```

And running INLA on this was fine. But permissions have changed in the newest stable version 23.04.24 and I can no longer run INLA models.

List of permissions below.

```
$ ls -lG /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/
...
-rwxrw-r-- 1 root 11989728 May  1 17:52 fmesher
-rwxrw-r-- 1 root      482 May  1 17:52 fmesher.run
-rwxrw-r-- 1 root 17712640 May  1 17:52 inla
-rwxrw-r-- 1 root 84591696 May  1 17:52 inla.mkl
-rwxrw-r-- 1 root     1384 May  1 17:52 inla.mkl.run
-rwxrw-r-- 1 root     1384 May  1 17:52 inla.run
...
```

If I brute force these permissions in my Dockerfile to mimic the original behaviour from INLA version 21.02.23, then all works fine in my singularity box.

But I was wondering if this change was intended behaviour (and why) or if the original permissions could be brought back in the next version.

Ubuntu machine info (where Docker and singularity images were created):

```
Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS (GNU/Linux 5.4.0-148-generic x86_64)
Docker version 20.10.21, build 20.10.21-0ubuntu1~20.04.2
singularity version 3.8.7
```

Minimally reproducible Dockerfile:

```
FROM rocker/r-ver:4.2.2

## Install packages
RUN apt-get update \
  && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    libgdal-dev \
    libproj-dev \
    libgeos-dev \
    lbzip2 \
    libnetcdf-dev \
    libsqlite3-dev \
    libssl-dev \
    libudunits2-dev \
    netcdf-bin \
    sqlite3 \
    imagemagick \
    pandoc \
    pandoc-citeproc \
    make \
    ghostscript \
    poppler-utils \
    zip \
    wget \
    fonts-dejavu-extra \
    curl \
    tk \
    xtide \
    openjdk-11-jre \
    gdebi-core \
    libfontconfig1-dev \
    libharfbuzz-dev \
    libfribidi-dev \
    cmake \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

## Install current INLA to ensure dependencies are installed.
## Use from MRAN (based on a date - YYYY-MM-DD)
RUN R -e "options(repos = \
    list(CRAN = 'http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/snapshot/2023-01-01/')); \
    install.packages('INLA',repos=c(getOption('repos'),INLA='https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable'), dep=TRUE); \
"

## Install more R packages versions from MRAN (based on a date - YYYY-MM-DD)
RUN R -e "options(repos = \
    list(CRAN = 'http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/snapshot/2023-01-01/')); \
  install.packages('inlabru'); \
  install.packages('R.utils'); \
  install.packages('sp'); \
"

### Install older version of INLA -- if using this option then
### cancel out the next block which changes executable permissions
# RUN  wget https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable/src/contrib/INLA_21.02.23.tar.gz \
#   && R CMD INSTALL --clean --no-multiarch --without-keep.source --byte-compile --resave-data --compact-docs --no-demo INLA_21.02.23.tar.gz \
#   && rm INLA_23.04.24.tar.gz

# Modify permissions for INLA executables
RUN chmod a+x /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher \
  && chmod a+x /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher.run \
  && chmod a+x /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla \
  && chmod a+x /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl \
  && chmod a+x /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl.run \
  && chmod a+x /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.run

WORKDIR /home/Project

## Default command to run
ENTRYPOINT ["Rscript"]
```

Build and run container interactively (takes an hour or more) -- fits model in INLA without issues:

```
$ docker build . --tag inlatest -f Dockerfile
$ docker save inlatest -o inlatest.tar
$ mkdir singularity_tmpdir
$ export SINGULARITY_TMPDIR=$PWD/singularity_tmpdir
$ TMPDIR=$PWD/singularity_tmpdir
$ singularity build inlatest.sif docker-archive://inlatest.tar
$ singularity shell inlatest.sif
$ ls -lG /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/
$ R
> library(INLA)
> summary(inla(y ~ 1, data = data.frame(y = rnorm(1e4))))
```

If I comment out the block in my Dockerfile that brute forces the permissions and then I update the singularity image, the above model call in R will fail with the following error message:

```
> summary(inla(y ~ 1, data = data.frame(y = rnorm(1e4))))
sh: 1: /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl.run: Permission denied
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

 *** inla.core.safe:  inla.program has crashed: rerun to get better initial values. try=1/2
sh: 1: /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl.run: Permission denied
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

 *** inla.core.safe:  inla.program has crashed: rerun to get better initial values. try=2/2
sh: 1: /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl.run: Permission denied
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.
Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)) :
  error in evaluating the argument 'object' in selecting a method for function 'summary': *** Fail to get good enough initial values. Maybe it is due to something else.
```

Hi Diego, the change was not intended. I will try to bring them back
by changing the permissions. Sometimes its a little hard to keep track
of all these and also how they they behave if you unpack a file on
another machine with different default settings like `umask`

So I guess you'll be safe to alter these manually in any case.

Hopefully you can use a new version of INLA as it will run much better
than the version from 2021....

All the best
Havard

messages.body_plain:
Dear all, hi.

Not exactly for an INLA application, but is there any way to calculate the distance between every mesh node pairs from inla.mesh.2d?

Suppose the following mesh:

library(INLA)

loc <- matrix(runif(10 * 2), 10, 2)

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc, offset = c(0.1, 0.2), max.edge = c(0.05, 0.1))

plot(mesh)

I would like to get the distance between all mesh nodes, but following the mesh lines. I have to calculate distance between geographical points but taking into account barriers. So it seems to me that constructing a mesh that follows a certain shape and then getting the distances between nodes would fit perfectly to this need.

All the best,

Silas

messages.subject: Interpreting simulation study model validation
messages.subject_clean: Interpreting simulation study model validation
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

I ran a simulation study to test the performance of a model according to Zuur et al., 2017 (Beginner's Guide to Spatial, Temporal and Spatial-Temporal Ecological Data Analysis with R-INLA). That involved generating 1000 simulated data sets from the model and comparing the number of zeros in the observed data set vs the number of zeros in the simulated data set.

The result of the study showed that the simulated data had a larger number of zeros compared to the observed data. What are the possible reasons that could contribute to this? missing covariates? zero inflation? I know each case is specific, but i would like to know of the potential reasons as part of a discussion of the results of the model.

Thanks in advance,
Sophie

messages.subject_clean: Simulating count data
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone, I'm doing a scenario thru simulations for my project. Basically, I'm working on a lattice data, with 300 cities in it. Here, I'm splitting the study region into east and west regions. Now, I want to use the result of the spatial variance of the whole study region I
calculated from a Besag model and then simulate a data set of counts such
that the spatial variance is half the spatial
variance of the original dataset for the east region and then twice the spatial variance of the original dataset for the west region.

My general idea is to directly simulate from the CAR random effect. But I don't know how to do this. Is there a function under INLA that does this? Or is there a better way to do this?

Thanks in advance!

messages.body_plain:
The data are fisheries-independent survey records that were very zero-inflated, so i thinned them a little. The study area is quite large (most of the NE Atlantic shelf area).

I tried the following formulations:
GLM (one variable only) - Overestimates no of zeros
GAM - Simulated data underestimate the number of zeros compared to observed (left skewed histogram)
GAMM - Simulated data estimate a similar number of zeros to observed (right skewed but still high numbers of simulated datasets overestimating)
Temporal GAMM  - Similar to GAMM, frequency plot of simulated data sets is a little more centred around the no of zeros in observed data
Temporal GAMM + SPDE - Overestimates

So i suppose it must be the SPDE term causing an issue then.... but the SPDE term does improve model according to DIC... What do you think?

Thanks again, i appreciate that so many things could be causing this problem.
Sophie

with the priors, usually the pc-priors for them works well.

There is also this new families,

which includes the neg.binomial, for which allow you to mode the zero-
probabilty (ie non-constant).

If the number of zero's is your aim, you do not need to consider the
DIC. You can also consider models that separate the 0's, so there is no
overlap, maybe it gets easier then.

Hi all,

I am trying to fit a model using the function lgcp from inlabru, including a random spatial field fitted as a 2d spde using pc priors, and one covariate (to begin with).  The model works relatively well if the covariate is fitted as a linear effect, however I can't get it to work if I try to fit the covariate as a non-linear effect.

I have tried model = "rw1" and "rw2" but for both of them I get an error

Error in inla.check.location(location[[r]], term = gp$random.spec[[r]]$term,  :
  Locations are too close for f(elevation, model="rw1", ...):  min(diff(sort(x)))/diff(range(x)) = 3.191e-08 < 1e-05
  You can fix this by some kind of binning, see ?inla.group
  If you want/need to bypass this check at your own risk, do
> m = get("inla.models", inla.get.inlaEnv())
> m$latent$rw1$min.diff = NULL
> assign("inla.models", m, inla.get.inlaEnv())

This error persists even when changing the mesh to larger or smaller triangles, and when subsampling the point data to 50% of the points and even 10% of the points, or if I try and fit the model just with the covariate, without the spatial field

I have also tried to model the covariate as a 1d spde with 3, 5, 10, and 50 integration points, with and without the 2d spatial field, but also no luck, I get the error

Error in names(marginals.random) <- names.random :
  'names' attribute [2] must be the same length as the vector [1]

  *** Fail to get good enough initial values. Maybe it is due to something else.

iinla: Giving up and returning last successfully obtained result for diagnostic purposes.

Code for the model and 1d and 2d spde below

mesh1D <- inla.mesh.1d(seq(min(elev$elevation)-40, max(elev$elevation)+40, length.out = 10),
                       boundary = "free")
# 1d spde
matern1D <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh1D,
                                prior.range = c(200, 0.01),
                                prior.sigma = c(2, 0.05)
)

matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,
                              alpha = 3/2,
                              prior.sigma = c(1, 0.05),
                              prior.range = c(500, 0.05)
)

# model components
ecomp <- coordinates ~ elevation(main = elev, model = matern1D) +
  mySmooth(coordinates, model = matern)

# run model

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Spatial covariates can have a dense set of values, so best to control the model resolution explicitly for rw1 and rw2 models; use e.g. mapper=bru_mapper(mesh1D)
for that.
But that’s effectively also what happens for the spde model you tried, so there may be something else going on as well.
Can you provide a runnable code file using the data you linked to?

Also, what inla and inlabru versions? Have you tried the inlabru devel version?

Finn

Hi Finn,

Yeah, sorry about that, last minute Friday message, I did not think it through.

I have downloaded the inlabru developement version and the latest INLA version, and now the 1d SPDE seems to work. However, I am finding it quite hard to parametrise the 2 spdes (the 1d and the 2d) as slightly changing the priors in one completely changes the posteriors of both. Do you know where I can find an example of how to use mapper=bru_mapper(mesh1D) with the rw2 model? I have tried to find examples online but unsuccessfully, and would like to try and compare it with the spde implementation. Runnable code with this  <https://www.dropbox.com/s/rdh0h5ynpcfycfy/ex_data.RDS?dl=1>data below just for reference, this now works with the 1d spde but not with the rw2.

####
library(inlabru)
library(INLA)
data <- readRDS("Data/ex_data.RDS")

elev <- data$elev
mesh <- data$mesh
setts <- data$data
samplers <- data$samplers

# create 1d mesh
mesh1D <- inla.mesh.1d(seq(min(elev$elevation)-40, max(elev$elevation)+40, length.out = 100),

                       boundary = "free")
# 1d spde
matern1D <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh1D,

                                prior.range = c(800, 0.01),
                                prior.sigma = c(1, 0.01)
)

# 2d spde

matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,
                              alpha = 3/2,

                              prior.range = c(500, 0.01),
                              prior.sigma = c(1, 0.01)
)

# model components

comp <- coordinates ~ elevation(main = elev, model = matern1D) +
  mySmooth(coordinates, model = matern)

# fit model
fit <- lgcp(comp, setts,

            domain = list(coordinates = mesh),
            samplers = samplers,
            options =
              list(
                bru_verbose = TRUE
                # control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb", strategy = "gaussian")
              )
)

summary(fit)
####

Many thanks!

I would like to extend the coregionalization model that is discussed in R-INLA book.
The model can be fitted as follows:
x(s) = alpha_1 + epsi (s),
y(s) = alpha_2 + beta*epsi(s) + u(s)
where epsi(s) and u(s) are latent gaussian processes with zero- mean GRF.

I want to extend this model to allow for spatially varying beta such that:
x(s) = alpha_1 + epsi (s),
y(s) = alpha_2 + beta(s)*epsi(s) + u(s)

I have tried many codes in inlabru, but unfortunately i ended up with error

here is the code using inlabru:

svc.comp_1 <- ~ -1 + alpha(NP_mid_jan$Station.ID, model = 'iid') + epsi(NP_coords.jan,weights = NP_mid_jan$NP,model = spde.O.jan)

svc.comp_2 <- ~ -1 + alpha2(O_mid_jan$Station.ID, model = 'iid') +
  u(O_coords.jan, weights = O_mid_jan$TM, model = spde.O.jan) + beta(NP_coords.jan, weights = epsi, model =spde.NP.jan)

formula_1 <- NP_mid_jan ~-1 + alpha + epsi
formula_2 <-  O_mide_jan ~ -1+ alpha2+u+beta

like_1 <- like("gaussian", formula = formula_1, data = NP_mid_jan, domain = list(coordinates = mesh))
like_2 <- like('gaussian', formula = formula_2, data = O_mid_jan, domain = list(coordinates =  mesh))

joint <- bru(list(svc.comp_1, svc.comp_2),like_1, like_2,   options = list(
  control.compute = list(waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE),
  verbose = TRUE))

followed with the following error:

  All covariate evaluations for 'epsi' are NULL; an intercept component was likely intended.

Warning in add_mapper(component$main, label = component$label, lhoods = lh,  :
  All covariate evaluations for 'beta' are NULL; an intercept component was likely intended.
  Implicit latent intercept component specification is deprecated since version 2.1.14.
  Use explicit notation '+ beta(1)' instead.
Error in rep(k, sum(nonzero)) : invalid 'times' argument
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In .Ops.recycle.ind(e2, len = l1) : longer object length
	is not a multiple of shorter object length
2: In .Ops.recycle.ind(e2, len = l1) : longer object length
	is not a multiple of shorter object length
3: In -1 + alpha2 + u :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

I do not understand where the problem is, any help to solve this error.

Thanks in Advance
Sylvia A. Shawky

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

one likely problem is that you're using "object$variable" to access
data for the components instead of just "variable".
Also, list(comp1,comp2) would only work if you pre-concerted the
component specifications to component object lists first.
Easiest solution to that is to defined them in a single specification.
Thirdly, you need to have proper spatial objects as input; either sp
or sf. Below i'll assume you have them as SpatialPointsDataFrame
objects, but if they are sf objects, then just replace "coordinates"
with "geometry" (and for that you may need to install the inlabru
development version instead of the CRAN version, as support for sf
objects has greatly expanded in the past few months).
Fourth, you cannot use a component as weight in another component;
only fixed data values can be used as weights. The beta*epsi
construction has to be done in the formula itself.
Fifth, you have a Gaussian observation model, so the "domain" argument
doesn't do anything (that's for Poisson point process models).

svc.comp <- ~ -1 +
  alpha(Station.ID, model = 'iid') +
  epsi(coordinates,weights = NP,model = spde.O.jan) +
  alpha2(Station.ID, model = 'iid') +
  u(coordinates, weights = TM, model = spde.O.jan) +
  beta(NP_coords.jan, model =spde.NP.jan)

formula_1 <- NP_mid_jan ~-1 + alpha + epsi

formula_2 <-  O_mide_jan ~ -1+ alpha2+u+beta*epsi

like_1 <- like("gaussian", formula = formula_1, data = NP_mid_jan)
like_2 <- like('gaussian', formula = formula_2, data = O_mid_jan)

joint <- bru(lsvc.comp,like_1, like_2,   options = list(

  control.compute = list(waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE),
  verbose = TRUE))

Finn

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

your group-specification for the Month component doesn't look right;
you've called inla.spde.make.index() to construct it, but with the
n.spde value for the field model.

It's not clear what model you intended to implement for Month, so hard
to say how to fix it.

Finn

On Mon, 24 Apr 2023 at 11:54, TheCorinna1994 <corinn...@hotmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear all,
>
> I have the following two indices:
>
> index.month<-inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde = spde$n.spde, n.group = months)
> index.year<-inla.spde.make.index("field.year", n.spde = spde$n.spde, n.group=years )
>
> and the following two stacks:
>
> stack.data<-inla.stack(data=list(rain=monthly.value$Rain),  A=list(A,1,1,1), effects=list(c(index.month, list(Intercept=1)),  Latitude=monthly.value$Latitude,   Year=monthly.value$Year, Month=monthly.value$Month), tag="data")
> stack.data2<-inla.stack(data=list(rain=monthly.value$Rain),  A=list(A,1,1,1), effects=list(c(index.year, list(Intercept=1)),  Latitude=monthly.value$Latitude,   Year=monthly.value$Year, Month=monthly.value$Month), tag="data2")
> stack.all<-inla.stack(stack.data, stack.data2)
>

> formula<-rain~-1+Intercept+as.factor(Month)+as.factor(Year)+Latitude+
>   f(field,model=spde, group = field.group, control.group = list(model="ar1"))+

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: marginals.fixed is always a df with 43 rows?
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] Re: marginals.fixed is always a df with 43 rows?
messages.body_plain:
The storage for "marginals.fixed" is a list of matrices containing the
estimated posterior density for each fixed effect in the model. The
two columns are x-values and density values at those x-values.

Finn

messages.subject: non-spatial evaluation of covars with _eval only fails when >1 covar present
messages.subject_clean: non-spatial evaluation of covars with _eval only fails when >1 covar present
messages.body_plain:
I have tried this with the gorillas dataset to make sure it's not an issue with my data or model. When we run a 1 covar model, we can evaluate the effect of the covariate using the suffix _eval in the formula call of the predict function. so, the below code would produce a prediction on the new values provided in the "data" argument

####
library(inlabru)
library(INLA)

data(gorillas, package = "inlabru")
nests <- gorillas$nests
mesh <- gorillas$mesh
boundary <- gorillas$boundary
gcov <- gorillas$gcov

elevation <- gcov$elevation
waterdist <- gcov$waterdist

ecomp <- coordinates ~ elev(elevation, model = "linear") +
  # wd(waterdist, model = "linear") +
  Intercept(1)

efit <- lgcp(ecomp, nests, samplers = boundary, domain = list(coordinates = mesh))

elev.pred <- predict(
  efit,
  data = data.frame(elevation = seq(0, 100, length.out = 1000)),
  formula = ~ elev_eval(elevation)
)
####

However, if I add the water distance component to the formula, and run the model with the two covariates, and then try the predict function, I get the following error

Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘over’ for signature ‘"data.frame", "SpatialPixelsDataFrame"’

Versions:
inlabru version: 2.7.0.9006
INLA version: 23.04.24

Is this expected behaviour? If it is, is there a way that I can evaluate and plot the effect of covariates in a model with multiple covariates?

Many thanks,

Hello everyone!

I have made a huge progress in my code and in using INLA since my last question here but now I have a question I would like to discuss with you because I don't really know what R is doing behind the code I wrote.

I built a stack for estimation with my spatial data, 2 covariates, the spatial effect and one random effect and then I built the prediction stack only with NA data, the same 2 covariates and the spatial effect because I'm not interested in using the random effects for prediction. However, honestly, I don't know what is the code actually running and I don't understand how is R not complaining about not having the random effect.

In another question here in the group I found that I could give the prediction stack a new level of the random effect: for exemple, my random effects go from level 1 to 24 and I associated the level 25 as a random effect in the prediciton stack. The thing is that I have results when I don't give any random effect and when I do, so I know something is going on behind the code but I can't justify or understand what is the right thing to do.

I appreciate any comments  and help you can give me on this subject!

Hope to year from you soon :)
Ema Biscaia

messages.subject: failing to fit random walk along year by location
messages.subject_clean: failing to fit random walk along year by location
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I'm trying to fit a dataset with multiple non-zero count data time series. About 250 locations, sampled once a month (6 winter months) during 30 years. About 34% of the design has a non-zero count. Every location has at least 5 years (8 observations) with non-zero counts, the median location as 18 years (49 observations) with non-zero counts.

The full model has a binomial component to fit the probability of non-zero counts. The idea is to fit a type 0 zero inflated distribution with a variable point mass of zero's.

The model (below the text) runs fine when I include a global trend (cyear), global seasonal effect (imonth), average location effect (location) and a change in season effect by year (imonth2).
I'd like to allow for a changing trend by location (cyear2). That model fails to fit. I get a bunch of "GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=46787". After some time the model is killed.

Any suggestions?

Best regards,

Thierry

inla(
  count ~ 0 + intercept +
    f(
      cyear, model = "rw1", scale.model = TRUE,
      hyper = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)))
    ) +
    f(
      cyear2, model = "rw1", constr = TRUE, replicate = ilocation,
      hyper = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)))
    ) +
    f(
      imonth, model = "rw1", constr = TRUE,
      hyper = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(0.5, 0.01)))
    ) +
    f(
      imonth2, model = "rw1", constr = TRUE, replicate = cyear,
      hyper = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(0.5, 0.01)))
    ) +
    f(
      location, model = "iid", constr = TRUE,
      hyper = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)))
    ),
  data = truncated_count, family = "zeroinflatednbinomial0",
  control.compute = list(config = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
  control.predictor = list(link = 1),
  control.family = list(
    list(hyper = list(theta2 = list(initial = -20, fixed = TRUE)))
  )
)

Somtimes these zero-inflated models can be a little tricky to get
started, is the likelihood can be not log-concave. you can force this
adding

	control.inla=list(cmin=0)

if this run goes well, can try to remove it with a rerun like

	r=inla(...,control.inla=list(cmin=0))
	r$.args$control.inla$cmin = -Inf
	r=inla.rerun(r)

btw, there is a new implementatino of the zeroinflated binomial and
poisson, which allow for more options, see

	inla.doc("0poisson")

nbinom, can be achived adding an iid random effect

if this does not help, please share so I can rerun it here

thx
H

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jonesmus,

The coefficients represent the increase in the expected log hazard for each covariate. You can get summary statistics for exp(coefficients) instead of coefficients (i.e. hazard ratios) by adding the following argument to the summary function: summary(model1, hazr=TRUE). Then the null effect is 1 and an effect is statistically significant at a significance level of 0.05 when the 95% credible interval does not contain 1.

Best,
Denis Rustand
he...@r-inla.org

messages.body_plain:
Dear Havard,

control.inla=list(cmin=0) doesn't solve the problem. The issue is probably with the data from some locations. Some locations have overall moderate counts (tens of individuals) in combination with one or two observations with high counts (thousands of individuals).
Some subsets fit without issues, other subsets fit with some messages "GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx". The subsets with a large portion of the data yield lots of "GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx" and fail to fit.
How can I capture the "GMRFLib_2order_approx" messages from the output? They are not present in the logfile.

The 0poisson is not an option. I use a more complex structure for the binomial part of the model. A zero trunctaced poisson and negative binomial distribution would be a nice thing to have.

Best regards,

ir. Thierry Onkelinx
Statisticus / Statistician

INSTITUUT VOOR NATUUR- EN BOSONDERZOEK / RESEARCH INSTITUTE FOR NATURE AND FOREST
Team Biometrie & Kwaliteitszorg / Team Biometrics & Quality Assurance

messages.subject: Interpretation of change in fixed effects after including spatial random effect
messages.subject_clean: Interpretation of change in fixed effects after including spatial random effect
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I am working with a logistic regression model.

First I ran the model with only fixed effects, and then I ran it including the spatial autocorrelation as a random effect (SPDE). Some of the fixed effect variables are binary and others are continuous (standardized).

Between both models the fixed effect A varies considerably. In the model without the random variable the mean is 0.026 and the credible interval includes the zero value (-0.608, 0.659). While in the model with random effect the mean is 1.140 and the credible interval does not include the zero value (0.169 , 2.166).

How can one interpret the change in the fixed effect A between both models? Is there a graphic I can make to help in the interpretation?

In the model with random effect, would the coefficient of the fixed effect A indicate the effect of A on the outcome variable when the other fixed effects take the value 0 and there is no spatial autocorrelation?

Thank you for your valuable time

Dario

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
In short, the two models are different, so the interpretation of the “effect of” A is different.. Most likely there is a spatial pattern in the data that is only partially captured by A, and when you include a random field that captures some of that pattern.  I’d suggest looking at spatial plots and residuals for the two models, to see if adding the random field reduces the spatial pattern structure in the residuals.

Finn

messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] Interpretation of change in fixed effects after including spatial random effect
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The interpretation most likely would depend on the nature of the
covariate; binary/continuous/geospatial or individual/etc.
If binary, and the model is
  E(y|model) = exp(beta_A * A + other + components)
then
  E(y|model, A=1) / E(y|model, A=0) = exp(beta_A)
assuming all other components are _unchanged_; they don't need to be zero.
I think that's the odd-ratio type interpretation you describe?

_However_:
If the covariate is inherently _spatial_, then the values of the other
components, in particular any random field, _cannot_ be unchanged,
since they would both depend on location, so this interpretation
doesn't really work.
This is an intrinsic problem with all complex structured models; the
simplistic interpretations from completely independent observation
models don't necessarily work anymore.
What I tend to do is to figure out what well-defined quantity I'm
interested in, and then compute that; this often involves computing
functionals of the model components, and not just the basic parameter
estimates.
E.g. the "intercept" is often not a good representation of the
"spatial average". To get to the actual spatial average, I'd compute
the posterior distribution of the integration average of
exp(predictor) instead.

Finn

messages.subject_clean: Difficulty in excuting inla results
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I am analysing spatial data using Bayesian framework. I have successfully created the adjacency matrix and all the necessary steps to develop the formula.
Using the INLA package, I found the following messages when I try to execute the results.
Any help, please?
This is the formula and codes I fitted.
-Formulaw <- Sa2_G2$case16_mb ~ Sa2_G2$Percentile + f(Sa2_G2$SA2_5DIG16, Sa2_G2$re_U, model = "besag", graph = "g8", scale.model = TRUE) + f(Sa2_G2$re_V, model = "iid")
-res <- inla(formula = Formulaw, family = "poisson", data = as.data.frame(Sa2_G2), E=Sa2_G2$Expected, control.predictor, list(compute=TRUE))
*** inla.core.safe: inla.program has crashed: rerun to get better initial values. try=2/2 Error in if (n.from.graph <= 0) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family, contrasts = contrasts, : *** Fail to get good enough initial values. Maybe it is due to something else.
